analysis:
The only change in this PR is in the live-only test file provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Live/Qwen/Qwen36ProductionCanaryTests.swift, head lines 389-391. It adds a `.toolCallDelta` case to the `switch` in `Qwen36ProductionCanary.collect`. The case appends `delta.completed` to `result.toolCalls` when present. The change is most likely a compile-fix for a new enum case in the server stream event type. No production code is touched in the supplied evidence.

I found no impact on the threat model. The test is gated by DARKBLOOM_LIVE_MLX_TESTS=1 and DARKBLOOM_LIVE_MLX_QWEN36=1, so it does not run by default. It handles only local model artifacts and fixture images, and exposes no network, key, attestation, authorization, billing, or cache-storage surface. The canary sets DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 for its bundles, so it does not exercise the SSD prefix cache (T-041). It does not change the coordinator-provider WebSocket contract (TB-002), A-001 plaintext handling, or the T-008 fail-closed encryption behavior.

The new streaming event `.toolCallDelta` is defined outside the supplied files, in MLXLMServer or the scheduler. Its production behavior and any tool-call fragment handling there were not visible. The next review pass should check those files if they changed in the same PR. Based on the supplied evidence, nothing in this unit is a security regression.
